records.source: וְהַנָּחָשׁ֙ הָיָ֣ה עָר֔וּם מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ף כִּֽי־אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן׃
records.gloss: And the serpent was crafty more than every animal of the field which had made YHWH God, and he said to the woman, indeed, that said God, not you will eat from every tree of the garden?
pieces: Now the serpent was more cunning than any wild animal {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God had made. It said to the woman, "Did God really tell you not to eat from any tree in the garden?"

L.1: Now the serpent was more crafty than every animal of the field that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God had made, and he said to the woman, "Did God really say, 'You shall not eat from any tree of the garden'?"

R.1: The snake was more clever and sly than any other wild animal {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God had made. It asked the woman, "Did God really tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?"

decisions.choice: crafty: shrewd, clever in a way that can serve good or bad ends
decisions.reason: The word can be praise, "prudent", as often in Proverbs (Proverbs 12:16, 23), or blame, "crafty" (Job 5:12). Here the serpent's cleverness is used to mislead. The word sounds like "naked" in the verse before (2:25): the man and woman are naked, the serpent is shrewd.

decisions.choice: the serpent: one of the animals God made, which speaks
decisions.reason: The serpent is described as one of the wild animals God made, and the text does not explain how it can speak or say who is behind it. Later scripture identifies "the ancient serpent" with the devil and Satan (Revelation 12:9; 20:2; compare John 8:44).

decisions.choice: did God really say: a question that twists the command
alternatives: a statement of surprise: so God has said ...!
decisions.reason: The words can be a question or an exclamation; either way they distort what God said. God allowed every tree but one (2:16-17); the serpent makes it sound as though he forbade them all. It also calls him only "God", not "the LORD God" as the narrator does.

decisions.choice: It (the serpent)
decisions.reason: Hebrew has no neuter, so the serpent is "he"; Balanced and Readable say "it", as English does for an animal. Literal keeps "he".

decisions.choice: snake
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word; "serpent" is the traditional one.

records.heading: The serpent and the forbidden tree

records.source: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־הַנָּחָ֑שׁ מִפְּרִ֥י עֵֽץ־הַגָּ֖ן נֹאכֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said the woman to the serpent, from [the] fruit of [the] tree[s] of the garden we will eat,
pieces: The woman answered the serpent, "We may eat fruit from the trees in the garden,

L.2: And the woman said to the serpent, "From the fruit of the trees of the garden we may eat,

R.2: The woman answered the snake, "We may eat fruit from the trees in the garden,

decisions.choice: we may eat: permission, not only what they do
decisions.reason: The verb form can describe what is done or what is allowed. The woman corrects the serpent: they may eat from the trees. She leaves out God's "every" and the generous "you may freely eat" (2:16).

records.source: וּמִפְּרִ֣י הָעֵץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתוֹךְ־הַגָּן֒ אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים לֹ֤א תֹֽאכְלוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְלֹ֥א תִגְּע֖וּ בּ֑וֹ פֶּן־תְּמֻתֽוּן׃
records.gloss: and from [the] fruit of the tree which [is] in [the] middle of the garden, said God, not you will eat from it, and not you will touch it, lest you die.
pieces: but about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden God said, 'You must not eat from it, and you must not touch it, or you will die.'"

L.3: but from the fruit of the tree that [is] in the middle of the garden, God said, 'You shall not eat from it, and you shall not touch it, lest you die.'"

R.3: but God said, 'Do not eat fruit from the tree in the middle of the garden. Do not even touch it, or you will die.'"

decisions.choice: and you shall not touch it: words not in God's command
decisions.reason: God's command in 2:17 said nothing about touching. The woman adds it, perhaps as a fence around the command, and she softens the warning from "you will surely die" to "or you will die". She also does not name the tree, calling it only "the tree in the middle of the garden" (see 2:9).

decisions.choice: lest you die: a warning of what will follow
decisions.reason: "Lest" introduces the result to be avoided. The verb carries an extra ending that adds weight to it.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַנָּחָ֖שׁ אֶל־הָֽאִשָּׁ֑ה לֹֽא־מ֖וֹת תְּמֻתֽוּן׃
records.gloss: And said the serpent to the woman, not dying you will die,
pieces: "You certainly will not die," the serpent said to the woman.

L.4: And the serpent said to the woman, "You will not surely die,

R.4: "You will not die," the snake told the woman.

decisions.choice: you will not surely die: the serpent denies God's own words
decisions.reason: The serpent repeats God's exact form of words from 2:17, "dying you will die", with "not" placed in front. It does not only question God's word now; it contradicts it.

decisions.choice: the serpent said, after the words
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the serpent's denial first, to give it the force it has in the Hebrew, where it answers the woman's last words directly.

records.source: כִּ֚י יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֗י בְּיוֹם֙ אֲכָלְכֶ֣ם מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְנִפְקְח֖וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם וִהְיִיתֶם֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים יֹדְעֵ֖י ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע׃
records.gloss: for knowing [is] God that in [the] day of your eating from it, and will be opened your eyes, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.
pieces: "God knows that when you eat from it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil."

L.5: for God knows that in the day you eat from it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil."

R.5: "God knows that when you eat it, your eyes will be opened. You will be like God. You will know good and evil."

decisions.choice: like God
decisions.reason: The word for God has a plural form and can mean "gods" or heavenly beings, and the following word "knowing" is plural, which could favor "like gods". But the serpent has just used the same word for God himself, and 3:22 ("like one of us") ties the knowledge to God. The serpent offers what belongs to God.

decisions.choice: your eyes will be opened: you will see and understand what you did not before
decisions.reason: The phrase is used for coming to see what was hidden (21:19; 2 Kings 6:17). It does come true in verse 7, but what they see is not what the serpent promised: they see that they are naked.

decisions.choice: God knows: the serpent suggests that God is holding something back
decisions.reason: The serpent presents God's command as jealous: God forbids the tree because he knows it would make them like him. The half-truth is the danger: their eyes are opened (verse 7) and they do gain a knowledge God has (verse 22), but they also die, as God said.

decisions.choice: no "for" at the start
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start a new quotation, since they ended the serpent's first words in verse 4; the Hebrew "for" joins the two halves of one speech.

records.source: וַתֵּ֣רֶא הָֽאִשָּׁ֡ה כִּ֣י טוֹב֩ הָעֵ֨ץ לְמַאֲכָ֜ל וְכִ֧י תַֽאֲוָה־ה֣וּא לָעֵינַ֗יִם וְנֶחְמָ֤ד הָעֵץ֙ לְהַשְׂכִּ֔יל וַתִּקַּ֥ח מִפִּרְי֖וֹ וַתֹּאכַ֑ל וַתִּתֵּ֧ן גַּם־לְאִישָׁ֛הּ עִמָּ֖הּ וַיֹּאכַֽל׃
records.gloss: And saw the woman that good [was] the tree for food, and that a delight it [was] to the eyes, and desirable [was] the tree to make wise, and she took from its fruit and ate, and she gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.
pieces: The woman saw that the tree was good for food, a delight to the eyes, and desirable for gaining wisdom. So she took some of its fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it.

L.6: And the woman saw that the tree [was] good for food, and that it [was] a delight to the eyes, and the tree [was] desirable to make [one] wise, and she took from its fruit and ate, and she gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.

R.6: The woman saw that the fruit of the tree looked good to eat. It was beautiful, and she wanted the wisdom it would give her. So she picked some fruit and ate it. Her husband was with her, and she gave some to him, and he ate it too.

decisions.choice: good for food, a delight to the eyes, desirable to make wise
decisions.reason: The three phrases describe how desire grows: the body, the eyes, the mind. The first two echo the trees God gave in 2:9, "pleasing to look at and good for food"; the third is what the serpent promised. 1 John 2:16 uses a similar three-part list.

decisions.choice: to make wise: to give insight, success
decisions.reason: The verb means to have or give insight and to act wisely and successfully. Some take it here as "to contemplate", but its usual sense, wisdom, fits the serpent's promise of knowledge.

decisions.choice: her husband with her: the man was there
alternatives: her husband, who joined her later
decisions.reason: "With her" places the man at the scene. He says nothing during the conversation, and he eats as she does.

decisions.choice: she wanted the wisdom it would give her
decisions.reason: Readable puts "desirable to make wise" in plain words, keeping the thought that the woman wanted what the serpent promised (m1, m2).

records.source: וַתִּפָּקַ֨חְנָה֙ עֵינֵ֣י שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י עֵֽירֻמִּ֖ם הֵ֑ם וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ֙ עֲלֵ֣ה תְאֵנָ֔ה וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם חֲגֹרֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And were opened [the] eyes of both of them, and they knew that naked they [were], and they sewed leaf[s] of fig and made for themselves loin coverings.
pieces: Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked. So they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for their waists.

L.7: And the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they [were] naked, and they sewed fig leaves together and made themselves loin coverings.

R.7: Then their eyes were opened, and they saw that they had no clothes on. So they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.

decisions.choice: their eyes were opened, and they knew they were naked: knowledge brings shame
decisions.reason: The serpent's promise comes true in a bitter way: their eyes are opened, and the first thing they know is that they are naked. In 2:25 they were naked and not ashamed; now they hide themselves from each other.

decisions.choice: loin coverings: something tied around the waist
decisions.reason: The word is used for a belt or a garment tied round the waist (2 Samuel 18:11). Their own covering is small and made of leaves; in verse 21 God gives them garments of skin.

records.source: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶת־ק֨וֹל יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּגָּ֖ן לְר֣וּחַ הַיּ֑וֹם וַיִּתְחַבֵּ֨א הָֽאָדָ֜ם וְאִשְׁתּ֗וֹ מִפְּנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים בְּת֖וֹךְ עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן׃
records.gloss: And they heard [the] sound of YHWH God walking about in the garden at [the] breeze of the day, and hid themselves the man and his wife from [the] face of YHWH God among [the] trees of the garden.
pieces: Then they heard the sound of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God walking in the garden at the breezy time of the day, and the man and his wife hid from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God among the trees of the garden.

L.8: And they heard the sound of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God walking about in the garden at the breeze of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God among the trees of the garden.

R.8: In the evening, when the breeze was blowing, they heard {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God walking in the garden. The man and his wife hid from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God among the trees.

decisions.choice: the sound of the LORD God walking
alternatives: the voice of the LORD God
decisions.reason: The word means sound or voice. Here it is the sound of God walking; in verse 10 the man says he heard "your sound".

decisions.choice: walking about in the garden: God is present with them
decisions.reason: The verb, in a form that means walking to and fro, is used later for God's presence among his people in the tabernacle camp (Leviticus 26:12; Deuteronomy 23:14). The story pictures God as near and at home in the garden.

decisions.choice: at the breeze of the day: in the cool of the evening, when the breeze rises
alternatives: in the storm wind of the day
decisions.reason: "The wind of the day" most likely means the time when the breeze comes up, in the afternoon or evening. Some read it as a stormy wind, a sign of God coming in judgment, but there is no other hint of a storm in the scene.

decisions.choice: In the evening, when the breeze was blowing
alternatives: at the breeze of the day
decisions.reason: Readable says what time of day is meant (m3).

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֛א יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ אַיֶּֽכָּה׃
records.gloss: And called YHWH God to the man and said to him, where [are] you?
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God called to the man, "Where are you?"

L.9: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God called to the man and said to him, "Where [are] you?"

R.9: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God called to the man, "Where are you?"

decisions.choice: where are you: a question that invites the man to come out
decisions.reason: God does not ask because he does not know. The question calls the man to answer and come out of hiding, as later questions (verses 11 and 13; 4:9) give him and the woman the chance to tell the truth.

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֶת־קֹלְךָ֥ שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בַּגָּ֑ן וָאִירָ֛א כִּֽי־עֵירֹ֥ם אָנֹ֖כִי וָאֵחָבֵֽא׃
records.gloss: And he said, your sound I heard in the garden, and I was afraid because naked I [was], and I hid myself.
pieces: He answered, "I heard {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sound in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked, so I hid."

L.10: And he said, "I heard {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sound in the garden, and I was afraid, because I [was] naked, and I hid myself."

R.10: The man answered, "I heard {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in the garden, and I was afraid because I was not wearing any clothes. So I hid."

decisions.choice: I was afraid because I was naked: fear and shame instead of trust
decisions.reason: The man gives fear and nakedness as his reasons, but not the eating. Their coverings of leaves do not take away his sense of being exposed before God.

decisions.choice: your (lowercase by default; Your with the setting)
decisions.reason: "You" and "your" when someone speaks to God take the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֚י הִגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עֵירֹ֖ם אָ֑תָּה הֲמִן־הָעֵ֗ץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר צִוִּיתִ֛יךָ לְבִלְתִּ֥י אֲכָל־מִמֶּ֖נּוּ אָכָֽלְתָּ׃
records.gloss: And he said, who told you that naked you [were]? From the tree which I commanded you not to eat from it, have you eaten?
pieces: God asked, "Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree I commanded you not to eat from?"

L.11: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Who told you that you [were] naked? Have you eaten from the tree from which I commanded you not to eat?"

R.11: God asked, "Who told you that you were naked? Did you eat fruit from the tree I told you not to eat from?"

decisions.choice: who told you ...? have you eaten ...?: God leads the man to the truth
decisions.reason: The first question shows that the knowledge of nakedness came from somewhere; the second names the tree. God gives the man the chance to confess.

decisions.choice: God asked
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, since the conversation now goes back and forth.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָֽאָדָ֑ם הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה עִמָּדִ֔י הִ֛וא נָֽתְנָה־לִּ֥י מִן־הָעֵ֖ץ וָאֹכֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said the man, the woman whom you put with me, she gave to me from the tree, and I ate.
pieces: The man said, "The woman {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put here with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it."

L.12: And the man said, "The woman whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put with me, she gave me [fruit] from the tree, and I ate."

R.12: The man said, "It was the woman {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put here with me. She gave me some fruit from the tree, and I ate it."

decisions.choice: the woman whom you put with me: the man blames the woman, and God
decisions.reason: The man puts the blame first on the woman and then, by "whom you put with me", on God himself. The woman he greeted with joy (2:23) is now "the woman". He admits his own part only at the end: "and I ate".

decisions.choice: [fruit]
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "she gave me from the tree"; Literal brackets the word English needs.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאִשָּׁ֖ה מַה־זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑ית וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה הַנָּחָ֥שׁ הִשִּׁיאַ֖נִי וָאֹכֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said YHWH God to the woman, what [is] this you have done? And said the woman, the serpent deceived me, and I ate.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said to the woman, "What is this that you have done?" The woman said, "The serpent tricked me, and I ate."

L.13: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said to the woman, "What [is] this you have done?" And the woman said, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate."

R.13: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said to the woman, "What have you done?" The woman answered, "The snake tricked me, and I ate the fruit."

decisions.choice: what is this you have done: a question of reproach
decisions.reason: The question is not a request for information but a rebuke, as when it is put to Abimelech or Laban (12:18; 29:25).

decisions.choice: deceived: led astray by lies
decisions.reason: The verb means to deceive or mislead. Paul uses this verse when he speaks of the serpent's deceit (2 Corinthians 11:3; 1 Timothy 2:14). The woman, like the man, passes on the blame, but what she says is true.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהֹוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֥ים׀אֶֽל־הַנָּחָשׁ֮ כִּ֣י עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּאת֒ אָר֤וּר אַתָּה֙ מִכָּל־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה וּמִכֹּ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה עַל־גְּחֹנְךָ֣ תֵלֵ֔ךְ וְעָפָ֥ר תֹּאכַ֖ל כָּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And said YHWH God to the serpent, because you have done this, cursed [are] you more than all the livestock and more than every animal of the field; on your belly you will go, and dust you will eat all [the] days of your life.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, you are cursed more than all the livestock and all the wild animals! You will crawl on your belly and eat dust all the days of your life.

L.14: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, cursed [are] you above all the livestock and above every animal of the field; on your belly you will go, and dust you will eat all the days of your life.

R.14: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said to the snake, "Because you did this, you are cursed more than any other animal, tame or wild. You will crawl on your belly, and you will eat dust as long as you live.

decisions.choice: cursed: placed under God's judgment, cut off from blessing
decisions.reason: To be cursed is the opposite of being blessed (1:22, 28): it means to be under judgment and cut off from good. God curses the serpent and the ground (verse 17), but not the man or the woman.

decisions.choice: on your belly you will go, and dust you will eat: a picture of utter humiliation
alternatives: a description of how snakes came to have no legs
decisions.reason: Crawling and eating dust is a picture of defeat and shame, used of enemies brought low (Psalm 72:9; Isaiah 65:25; Micah 7:17). The verse need not mean that snakes once had legs; it gives the serpent's way of moving a meaning.

decisions.choice: because you have done this: the serpent is not questioned
decisions.reason: God asks the man and the woman to explain themselves, but not the serpent; he pronounces judgment on it at once. The judgments then come in reverse order: serpent, woman, man.

records.source: וְאֵיבָ֣ה׀אָשִׁ֗ית בֵּֽינְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין זַרְעָ֑הּ ה֚וּא יְשׁוּפְךָ֣ רֹ֔אשׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה תְּשׁוּפֶ֥נּוּ עָקֵֽב׃ס
records.gloss: And enmity I will put between you and between the woman, and between your offspring and between her offspring; he will strike you [on the] head, and you will strike him [on the] heel.
pieces: I will make you and the woman enemies, and your offspring and hers. He will strike your head, and you will strike his heel."

L.15: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel."

R.15: I will make you and the woman enemies. Your children and her children will be enemies too. One of her children will crush your head, and you will bite his heel."

decisions.choice: enmity: lasting hostility, as between enemies
decisions.reason: The word is used for deep hostility that leads to violence (Numbers 35:21-22). God himself sets the enmity: the woman and the serpent will not be allies.

decisions.choice: offspring: descendants, either many or one
alternatives: seed (in the sense of a family line)
decisions.reason: The word, literally "seed", can mean a whole line of descendants or a single child (4:25). The first half of the sentence speaks of two lines in conflict; the second narrows to "he" and "you".

decisions.choice: he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel: a struggle in which the serpent receives the deadly blow
alternatives: the ongoing fight between people and snakes, with no further sense
a promise of one descendant of the woman who will defeat the serpent
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for both blows; it means to strike or crush. A blow to the head is deadly; a bite on the heel is painful but not final. The pronoun "he" and his "heel" are singular, and the Septuagint keeps a masculine "he". Jewish and Christian readers have long heard a promise here, and Christians read it as the first announcement of the gospel, fulfilled in Christ's victory over Satan (Romans 16:20; Revelation 12:9). The verse itself speaks of the woman's offspring, without naming one person.

decisions.choice: strike
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses one verb for both blows (m3). Balanced uses one English verb for both, "strike"; Readable says "crush" and "bite" to show what each blow is.

decisions.choice: One of her children
decisions.reason: Readable names the "he" as one of the woman's descendants, which is what the singular pronoun refers to, without deciding who it is (m3).

records.source: אֶֽל־הָאִשָּׁ֣ה אָמַ֗ר הַרְבָּ֤ה אַרְבֶּה֙ עִצְּבוֹנֵ֣ךְ וְהֵֽרֹנֵ֔ךְ בְּעֶ֖צֶב תֵּֽלְדִ֣י בָנִ֑ים וְאֶל־אִישֵׁךְ֙ תְּשׁ֣וּקָתֵ֔ךְ וְה֖וּא יִמְשָׁל־בָּֽךְ׃ס
records.gloss: To the woman he said, increasing I will increase your pain and your pregnancy; in pain you will bear children, and toward your husband [will be] your desire, and he will rule over you.
pieces: To the woman {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I will greatly increase your pain in childbearing; with pain you will give birth to children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you."

L.16: To the woman {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I will surely increase your pain and your pregnancy; in pain you will bear children, and your desire [will be] for your husband, and he will rule over you."

R.16: Then God said to the woman, "I will make having babies very painful for you, and you will give birth in pain. You will long for your husband, and he will rule over you."

decisions.choice: your pain and your pregnancy: the pain of pregnancy and childbirth
decisions.reason: Two nouns joined by "and" often express one idea in Hebrew. The next line makes clear that the pain of bearing children is meant. The word for pain is the same as the man's "painful toil" in verse 17: both now carry out their callings (1:28) in pain.

decisions.choice: your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you: a relationship bent by the fall
alternatives: your desire will be to control your husband, but he will rule over you
your longing for your husband will lead to his ruling over you
decisions.reason: The word for desire is used only twice more: of a man's love for a woman (Song of Songs 7:10) and of sin's desire to master Cain, which he must rule over (4:7). Read with 4:7, it is a desire to control; read with the Song, it is longing. Either way, the verse describes a relationship spoiled by sin, with rule where there had been partnership (2:18-24). It describes what will happen, not what God commands.

decisions.choice: pain in childbearing (B); having babies very painful (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the two nouns into one idea (m1); Literal keeps both.

records.source: וּלְאָדָ֣ם אָמַ֗ר כִּֽי־שָׁמַעְתָּ֮לְק֣וֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ֒ וַתֹּ֨אכַל֙ מִן־הָעֵ֔ץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוִּיתִ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֲרוּרָ֤ה הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּֽעֲבוּרֶ֔ךָ בְּעִצָּבוֹן֙ תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֔נָּה כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And to [the] man he said, because you listened to [the] voice of your wife and ate from the tree which I commanded you, saying, not you will eat from it, cursed [is] the ground because of you; in painful toil you will eat [from] it all [the] days of your life.
pieces: To the man {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree I commanded you not to eat from, the ground is cursed because of you. Through painful work you will eat from it all the days of your life.

L.17: And to the man {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Because you listened to the voice of your wife and ate from the tree about which I commanded you, saying, 'You shall not eat from it,' cursed [is] the ground because of you; in painful toil you will eat [from] it all the days of your life.

R.17: Then God said to the man, "You listened to your wife and ate fruit from the tree I told you not to eat from. Because of what you did, I am putting a curse on the ground. You will have to work very hard all your life to grow food from it.

decisions.choice: to the man: not yet the name Adam
decisions.reason: As in 2:20, the Hebrew vowels give the word without the article, so it can be read as the name Adam. The story still calls him "the man" in verses 20-24, and the name is plainly used from 4:25, so it is taken as "the man".

decisions.choice: cursed is the ground because of you: the man's work is made hard
decisions.reason: God does not curse the man; he curses the ground, the man's own source (2:7) and the place of his work (2:15). Work was good before; now it becomes painful toil. Romans 8:20-22 speaks of the whole creation subjected to frustration and waiting to be set free.

decisions.choice: painful toil: hard, wearying labor
decisions.reason: The word is related to "pain" in childbearing (verse 16) and returns when Lamech names his son Noah, hoping for relief from "the painful toil of our hands" from the cursed ground (5:29).

decisions.choice: listened to the voice of your wife: obeyed her
decisions.reason: "Listen to the voice of" means to obey (as in 22:18; Exodus 15:26). The fault is not that the man heard his wife but that he obeyed her instead of God.

decisions.choice: I am putting a curse on the ground
decisions.reason: Readable makes the passive active, naming God as the one who curses, as the context makes clear.

records.source: וְק֥וֹץ וְדַרְדַּ֖ר תַּצְמִ֣יחַֽ לָ֑ךְ וְאָכַלְתָּ֖ אֶת־עֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And thorn[s] and thistle[s] it will make sprout for you, and you will eat [the] plants of the field.
pieces: It will grow thorns and thistles for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.

L.18: And thorns and thistles it will make sprout for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.

R.18: Thorns and weeds will grow from it, and you will eat the plants that grow in the fields.

decisions.choice: thorns and thistles: weeds that fight against the farmer
decisions.reason: The pair stands for the weeds and briars that choke crops; Hosea 10:8 uses it of ruined land. The ground that God made to grow good plants (1:11-12) now also grows what makes work hard.

decisions.choice: the plants of the field: the crops a farmer grows
decisions.reason: These are the cultivated plants missing in 2:5 for lack of someone to work the ground. The man will eat, but by farming, not by picking fruit from the garden's trees.

records.source: בְּזֵעַ֤ת אַפֶּ֨יךָ֙ תֹּ֣אכַל לֶ֔חֶם עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ כִּֽי־עָפָ֣ר אַ֔תָּה וְאֶל־עָפָ֖ר תָּשֽׁוּב׃
records.gloss: By [the] sweat of your face you will eat bread until your return to the ground, for from it you were taken; for dust you [are], and to dust you will return.
pieces: You will eat bread by the sweat of your brow until you return to the ground, because you were taken from it. You are dust, and to dust you will return."

L.19: By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground, for from it you were taken; for you [are] dust, and to dust you will return."

R.19: You will sweat as you work to get food to eat, until you die and return to the ground. You were made from the ground. You came from dust, and you will go back to dust."

decisions.choice: by the sweat of your face you will eat bread: food will cost hard labor
decisions.reason: "Bread" stands for food in general. The sweat of the face is the sweat of hard work.

decisions.choice: dust you are, and to dust you will return: death
decisions.reason: God's warning in 2:17 is fulfilled: the man will die and return to the ground he was taken from (2:7). Ecclesiastes 3:20 and 12:7 and Psalm 90:3 take up the same words.

decisions.choice: brow
decisions.reason: "Sweat of your brow" is the English way of saying what the Hebrew calls "the sweat of your face"; Literal keeps "face".

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֧א הָֽאָדָ֛ם שֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ חַוָּ֑ה כִּ֛י הִ֥וא הָֽיְתָ֖ה אֵ֥ם כָּל־חָֽי׃
records.gloss: And called the man [the] name of his wife Eve, because she was [the] mother of every living [one].
pieces: The man named his wife Eve, because she would become the mother of all the living.

L.20: And the man called his wife's name Eve, because she was the mother of all living.

R.20: The man named his wife Eve, which sounds like the Hebrew word for "living," because she would be the mother of all people.

decisions.choice: Eve (Chawwah): a name that sounds like "living"
decisions.reason: The name sounds like the Hebrew word for life or living. After the sentence of death (verse 19), the man gives his wife a name of life: through her, human life will go on.

decisions.choice: she was the mother: she would become the mother
decisions.reason: The verb is in a completed form, but she has no children yet (4:1). It looks ahead, as a statement of what she would be, or it is the narrator's explanation of the name.

decisions.choice: which sounds like the Hebrew word for "living"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the play on words that gives the name its point (m1).

records.source: וַיַּעַשׂ֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְאָדָ֧ם וּלְאִשְׁתּ֛וֹ כָּתְנ֥וֹת ע֖וֹר וַיַּלְבִּשֵֽׁם׃פ
records.gloss: And made YHWH God for [the] man and for his wife garments of skin, and he clothed them.
pieces: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made garments of skin for the man and his wife, and clothed them.

L.21: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made for the man and for his wife garments of skin, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} clothed them.

R.21: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dressed them.

decisions.choice: garments of skin, and he clothed them: God's care after judgment
decisions.reason: God replaces the coverings of leaves (verse 7) with lasting clothes and dresses them himself, an act of care even as they are sent out. The text does not explain how the skins were obtained.

decisions.choice: for the man: again without the article
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, the word can be read as the name Adam; it is taken as "the man" (see 2:20).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים הֵ֤ן הָֽאָדָם֙ הָיָה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לָדַ֖עַת ט֣וֹב וָרָ֑ע וְעַתָּ֣ה׀פֶּן־יִשְׁלַ֣ח יָד֗וֹ וְלָקַח֙ גַּ֚ם מֵעֵ֣ץ הַֽחַיִּ֔ים וְאָכַ֖ל וָחַ֥י לְעֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And said YHWH God, behold, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil; and now, lest he stretch out his hand and take also from [the] tree of the life and eat and live forever —
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said, "The man has now become like one of {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}}, knowing good and evil. He must not be allowed to reach out his hand and take from the tree of life as well, and eat, and live forever."

L.22: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said, "Look, the man has become like one of {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}}, knowing good and evil; and now, lest he stretch out his hand and take also from the tree of life and eat, and live forever —"

R.22: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God said, "The man has become like {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}}. He knows good and evil. Now he must not reach out and take fruit from the tree that gives life, and eat it, and live forever."

decisions.choice: like one of us: God speaks in the plural, as in 1:26
alternatives: like one of the heavenly beings
decisions.reason: As in 1:26, God speaks in the plural; the possible readings are the same (see 1:26, m1). The serpent's promise (verse 5) has come true in part: the man knows good and evil, but as one who has disobeyed.

decisions.choice: lest he ... and live forever: the sentence breaks off
decisions.reason: God's words stop in the middle of the sentence, and the action of verse 23 completes it: God sends the man out. Living forever in a broken state is kept from him; the tree of life returns in Revelation 22:2, 14.

decisions.choice: a dash at the end
decisions.reason: Literal ends with a dash to show that God's sentence breaks off (m2); Balanced and Readable complete it with "must not".

decisions.choice: us (lowercase by default; Us with the setting)
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself, so "us" takes the deity pronoun setting, as in 1:26.

records.heading: Sent out of the garden

records.source: וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֛הוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִגַּן־עֵ֑דֶן לַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֻקַּ֖ח מִשָּֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And sent him out YHWH God from [the] garden of Eden to work the ground from where he was taken.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God sent him out of the garden of Eden to work the ground he had been taken from.

L.23: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God sent him out from the garden of Eden to work the ground from which he was taken.

R.23: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God sent the man out of the garden of Eden to farm the ground he had been made from.

decisions.choice: sent him out: dismissed him from the garden
decisions.reason: The verb is the same as "stretch out" his hand in verse 22: lest the man send out his hand, God sends out the man. It is used for sending someone away for good (Deuteronomy 24:1).

decisions.choice: to work the ground: the work of 2:15 continues outside the garden
decisions.reason: The man still works the ground, as he was made to (2:5, 15), but now outside the garden and from the cursed ground (verse 17).

records.source: וַיְגָ֖רֶשׁ אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁכֵּן֩ מִקֶּ֨דֶם לְגַן־עֵ֜דֶן אֶת־הַכְּרֻבִ֗ים וְאֵ֨ת לַ֤הַט הַחֶ֨רֶב֙ הַמִּתְהַפֶּ֔כֶת לִשְׁמֹ֕ר אֶת־דֶּ֖רֶךְ עֵ֥ץ הַֽחַיִּֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And he drove out the man, and he stationed east of [the] garden of Eden the cherubim and the flame of the sword the whirling to guard [the] way [to the] tree of the life.
pieces: After {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drove the man out, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} placed cherubim on the east side of the garden of Eden, with a flaming sword that turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life.

L.24: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drove out the man, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stationed east of the garden of Eden the cherubim and the flame of the whirling sword, to guard the way to the tree of life.

R.24: God forced the man to leave. On the east side of the garden of Eden {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put mighty angels called cherubim, and a flaming sword that flashed back and forth. They guarded the way to the tree that gives life.

decisions.choice: cherubim: heavenly guardians of God's presence
alternatives: winged infants, as in later art
decisions.reason: Cherubim are powerful winged beings who guard holy places. Figures of cherubim stood over the ark of the covenant and were woven into the curtain of the tabernacle (Exodus 25:18-22; 26:31). Like the entrance to the tabernacle and the temple, the garden is entered from the east, and the way is guarded.

decisions.choice: the flame of the whirling sword: a flashing, turning blade of fire
alternatives: a sword held by the cherubim
decisions.reason: The text sets the sword beside the cherubim without saying that they hold it. The verb pictures it turning this way and that, so that no way past is left open.

decisions.choice: to guard the way: to keep watch over the path
decisions.reason: The verb is the man's "keep" of 2:15: the garden he was set to keep is now kept against him.

decisions.choice: mighty angels called cherubim
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the cherubim are (m1).

decisions.choice: God forced the man to leave
decisions.reason: Readable names God and puts "drove out" plainly.
